question_text: Which are the areas you must not drive into when there is traffic congestion?

options.text: Crossroads
Level crossings
Driveways

correct_answers.text: Crossroads
Level crossings

comment: In the case of stagnant traffic, the following areas must be kept free for example for emergency vehicles: intersections, level crossings and cross-walks. For residential exits, this rule does not apply. If you notice that someone wants to drive off his property onto the road, you should give the driver the opportunity to enter the road.

question_text: Which are the areas you must not drive into when there is traffic congestion?

options.text: Junctions
Pedestrian crossings
'Bus stops with "zig-zag lines"'

correct_answers.text: Junctions
Pedestrian crossings

comment: If traffic slows down, you may only enter intersections if you can leave them quickly. Otherwise you have to wait. Also, junctions of cross streets, cross-walks and level crossings are to be kept free. However, this does not apply to bus stops.

options.text: Reduce speed and, if necessary, stop
Proceed, pulling over onto the pavement
Speed up and proceed since the oncoming traffic must wait

correct_answers.text: Reduce speed and, if necessary, stop

comment: Due to the traffic sign you have to wait here. The red arrow in your direction indicates that priority is given to oncoming vehicles. In no case may you drive onto the sidewalk. This is reserved solely for pedestrians.

question_text: During traffic congestion, what parts of the road infrastructure must be kept clear?

options.text: Traffic confluences
Pedestrian crossings
Bus stops

correct_answers.text: Traffic confluences
Pedestrian crossings

comment: The pedestrian crossing (“zebra crossing”) is intended to enable pedestrians to cross the road safely and without danger. For this reason, you must leave pedestrian crossings free under all circumstances. If you drive into a junction (or crossing) in slow-moving traffic, there is a risk that you will block oncoming cross traffic or that oncoming traffic turning left will have to wait unnecessarily long. The junction or crossing would thus become even more clogged and traffic would be obstructed more than necessary.

question_text: You want to continue driving straight ahead. What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I allow the convoy to pass through
I wait at the stop line
I cross over the junction

correct_answers.text: I allow the convoy to pass through
I wait at the stop line

comment:
A group of pedestrians, cyclists or motor vehicles, which is traveling together in road traffic, is called a closed association. Closed associations must be clearly marked and must not be interrupted.
So you have to wait until all vehicles drove past you and as long as you have to wait at the stop line.

question_text: You want to continue driving straight ahead. What is the right course of action?

options.text: I remain waiting in my lane
I move to the right if there is sufficient space in the traffic
I overtake the vehicle alongside me and switch lanes

correct_answers.text: I remain waiting in my lane
I move to the right if there is sufficient space in the traffic

comment: The car ahead blocks you in your lane. Nevertheless, you should not overtake on the right before the intersection, as this would be too dangerous. Keep your distance, reduce the speed and stop if necessary. Continue straight ahead when the free lane is free and the traffic light turns green. You can only change on the right lane if there is a sufficiently large traffic gap.

options.text: Stop before the left turn and keep the central divide clear
Turn smoothly, so as not to impede following traffic
Come to a stop in the central divide, where the other car is stopped

correct_answers.text: Stop before the left turn and keep the central divide clear

comment: If tram rails lead through the left turn lane and you want to turn left when the tram approaches, it is important to wait with sufficient distance in front of the tram rails. When the tram passed, you can turn left.

question_text: What is the right course of action?

options.text: Slow down
Accelerate
Swerve to the left

correct_answers.text: Slow down

comment: If a cyclist who moves to the left drives in front of you, you must not overtake him if the road is narrowed at this point and there is oncoming traffic. A safety distance of 1.5 to 2 meters could not be maintained here.

question_text: What is the right course of action?

options.text: Slow down
Accelerate
Swerve to the left

correct_answers.text: Slow down

comment: On your side the road narrows. The cyclist will therefore move to the left. Because of oncoming traffic, you cannot overtake him with the required safety distance of 1.5 to 2 meters. That's why you have to wait and stay behind him.

question_text: In which situations are you not allowed to enter a junction even though the traffic light is green?

options.text: If I would have to stop in the middle of the junction because the traffic is backing up
If asked to stop by a police officer
If the sign "Stop. Give way" is displayed at the junction

correct_answers.text: If I would have to stop in the middle of the junction because the traffic is backing up
If asked to stop by a police officer

comment: In the following cases, you must not enter a crossroad, even though the traffic light shows "green": with slow-moving traffic, as crossings, for example, must remain free for emergency vehicles. Secondly, when police officers regulate traffic and give instructions that deviate from the meanings of the colors of the traffic lights. In general, a green traffic light tells you that you are allowed to drive and overrules other traffic signs that regulate the right of way. Policeman orders have the highest rank and override traffic lights.

question_text: In what instances may you not enter a junction, even though you have right of way?

options.text: - would have to wait in the junction because the traffic in my direction is backing up
- would impede a vehicle with flashing blue lights and siren
- want to turn left and would have to wait in the junction because of oncoming traffic

correct_answers.text: - would have to wait in the junction because the traffic in my direction is backing up
- would impede a vehicle with flashing blue lights and siren

comment: If the traffic slows down, you may enter a crossroad with a green traffic light or right of way only if you can leave it quickly without blocking it. This is particularly important in order to keep the intersection free for police, fire and ambulance emergency vehicles. If you hear a siren, you have to drive carefully to the crossroad and may only continue if you hinder no emergency vehicle. When turning left, you must slowly enter the intersection and wait there until you can drive freely without oncoming traffic.

question_text: Why must you slow down here and be ready to brake?

options.text: - cyclist
- [green] vehicle
- pedestrian

correct_answers.text: - cyclist

comment: You don't have to slow down because of pedestrians. He is far enough away from the constriction. The red vehicle is standing and is therefore no reason to slow down as well. However, reduce the speed because of the cyclist. He could change lanes without a hand signal and bring about a dangerous situation.

question_text: Why do you have to continue to brake?

options.text: - refuse truck
- blue truck
- cyclist

correct_answers.text: - refuse truck
- blue truck

comment: A garbage truck comes towards the blue truck and forces him to stop. Since the garbage truck could swing out and get on your lane as it turns, you'll need to wait for the vehicle to be properly merged. The cyclist is no reason for braking.

question_text: You want to drive straight ahead. What should you do?

options.text: - at the stop line
- between the yellow and the blue vehicle
- directly behind the yellow vehicle

correct_answers.text: - at the stop line

comment: In case of halting traffic, you are not allowed to block any intersection or T-junction despite the green traffic light or right of way. You may need to wait at the stop line and cannot close up until the front vehicles are far enough away.

options.text: Once the truck driver has made a hand signal clearly yielding his right of way
If I do not endanger or significantly impede the cross traffic
Immediately because the truck driver is urging me to do so

correct_answers.text: Once the truck driver has made a hand signal clearly yielding his right of way
If I do not endanger or significantly impede the cross traffic

comment: The truck was signaled by flasher that he waives his right of way. Therefore, is after the truck driver has clearly waived with hands on his priority right and if you do not endangering the cross traffic or not substantially behinderst.

question_text: When may you take the turn?

options.text: Only once the truck driver has used a hand signal to clearly indicate he is foregoing his right of way
Only if I do not endanger or significantly impede the cross traffic
Immediately, because the truck driver is prompting me to do that

correct_answers.text: Only once the truck driver has used a hand signal to clearly indicate he is foregoing his right of way
Only if I do not endanger or significantly impede the cross traffic

comment: As you want to turn left, oncoming traffic has priority. Only when the lorry driver gives up his right of way with a clear hand signal can you pass with due regard for oncoming traffic. Flashing your lights is not sufficient here.

question_text: You want to drive straight ahead. What should you do if the [red] truck immediately drives off on “green”?

options.text: I wait and allow the truck to move off
I give a warning signal if necessary
I also drive off immediately

correct_answers.text: I wait and allow the truck to move off
I give a warning signal if necessary

comment: You should wait here and let the truck move off, giving warning signs if necessary as it appears to be turning right. (Turn signal right)

question_text: You want to drive straight ahead. Where should you position yourself in this situation?

options.text: On the right behind the truck
On the left behind the truck
Directly behind the motorbike

correct_answers.text: On the right behind the truck

comment: The truck swerves to turn right, wait until the turn is completed. Then you can drive straight ahead.
